runs.text: Sixty seven words. One letter. And the map of the Middle East changed. November two, one thousand nine hundred and seventeen. In the middle of World War One, Britain's foreign secretary, Arthur Balfour, writes to Lord Rothschild. Britain views with favour a national home for the Jewish people, in Palestine. Weeks later, British troops march into Jerusalem. In nineteen twenty two, the League of Nations writes the promise into Britain's mandate for Palestine. But read the second half. Nothing may harm the civil and religious rights of the non Jewish communities. And nothing may harm the rights of Jews in any other country. Thirty one years later, Israel is born. Palestinian leaders see it as a promise made without them. In twenty seventeen, Mahmoud Abbas said Britain must recognise its mistakes. A promise kept, or a promise broken? Tell me below. And all of it began with sixty seven words.
